products.name: PlateCost: Menu Item Cost and Price Calculator
products.unique_concept: Plate-costing tool that adds packaging, waste/trim yield and non-ingredient overhead to ingredient cost, and shows the price needed for a target margin rather than only a food-cost percentage.
products.pain_points: Prices set by gut; ingredient cost jumps; costing software $15-250/mo
products.pitch_points: Know true plate cost; reprice when suppliers change; no subscription
features: Ingredient library (unit, pack price, yield %)
Recipe builder with portions, packaging, waste %
Overhead per plate (user-entered) and target margin
Price needed = total cost / (1 - target margin) and resulting food-cost %
Bulk supplier price change (+x%) re-cost of all items
Printable cost sheet, CSV/JSON export, localStorage
products.build_spec: Single-file HTML. ingredient_cost_per_unit = pack_price/(pack_qty x yield); plate_cost = sum(qty x unit_cost) + packaging + overhead_per_plate; price = plate_cost/(1 - margin); food_cost_pct = ingredient_part/price. No assumed benchmark % (30% shown only as editable example). Unit tests + phone width.

novelty_check.vs_memory: no overlap with memory/products.json or daily 2026-11-24/25 products (builder-menumaker is a restaurant website builder, not costing)

products.score_note: self-scored from evidence cards; confidence Med/Low where noted

products.name: Price Hike Reality Check
products.unique_concept: Calculator showing how many covers/orders you can lose before a menu price increase hurts profit, and the profit change under your own volume-drop assumption; no elasticity claims.
products.pain_points: Fear of the pricing ceiling; unsure whether to raise prices
products.pitch_points: Decide price moves with numbers; break-even volume loss at a glance
features: Inputs: price, unit cost, weekly units, proposed increase %
Break-even volume loss % = 1 - (old margin / new margin)
Scenario table with user volume-drop %
Whole-menu mode (weighted by units)
Printable one-page summary
products.build_spec: Single-file HTML. unit_margin = price - cost; new_margin = price(1+h) - cost; break_even_loss = 1 - unit_margin/new_margin; profit_new = new_margin x units x (1-drop). Unit tests. README states: James Beard report says >10% hikes were linked with lower expected profit (survey, not causation).
